report.tagline: Google's UPI payments app in India, number two behind PhonePe, built on rewards, a clean design and Google's trust.
report.simpleSummary: Google Pay, or GPay, is one of the two apps most Indians use to pay with UPI. You can scan a QR code at a shop, send money to friends by phone number, split bills and pay electricity or phone bills. It grew fast in its early years by giving scratch-card rewards for paying friends. It is free for most payments; Google earns from bill fees, loans it helps arrange, merchant services and, from 2026, a new fee on bigger merchant payments.

overview.whatItDoes: Google Pay lets users in India make UPI payments to people and shops, pay bills and recharges, and apply for loans and credit cards from partner banks. Merchants use Google Pay for Business and QR codes, plus a SoundPod speaker in some areas. Google uses GPay to reach Indian users and businesses, and India is also where Google tests new payment ideas for the world.
howItWorks: Download GPay, verify your phone number and link a bank account with a UPI PIN.
Pay by scanning any UPI QR, entering a phone number or UPI ID, or tapping a contact.
Rewards like scratch cards and cashback appear after some payments.
Pay bills and recharges; card-funded bill payments carry a small convenience fee.
Apply for personal loans, gold loans and co-branded credit cards from partner banks.
UPI Circle lets a trusted person, like a parent, pay from your account with limits.
overview.valueProposition: A simple, trusted way to pay anyone in India, backed by Google, with occasional rewards.

businessModel.summary: Google Pay earns very little directly from UPI payments because the government has banned fees on most of them. It makes money from convenience fees on card-funded bill payments, commissions on loans and credit cards, merchant services and ads, and gains strategic value by keeping Google close to Indian users. A new 0.4 percent fee on larger merchant UPI payments, announced in 2026, could give it real revenue.

revenueStreams.detail: About 0.5 to 1 percent plus GST on bill payments made with credit or debit cards, introduced in 2025.
Fees from partner banks and NBFCs for loans and co-branded cards.
A 0.4 percent fee on eligible merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000, with small merchants exempt, start reportedly postponed to after Diwali 2026.
Brands pay to place coupons and offers in GPay.
Data and engagement that help Google's wider business in India, like Android, Ads and Play.

businessModel.pricing: UPI payments are free for users and most merchants. Card-funded bill payments carry a convenience fee of about 0.5 to 1 percent plus GST. Loans and cards follow partner pricing.
costDrivers: Servers and engineering for billions of payments
Merchant acquisition and partner bank fees
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a normal ₹200 UPI payment, Google Pay earns ₹0 and pays a small cost to process it. On a ₹10,000 credit card bill paid with another card, it might earn about ₹50 to ₹100 in convenience fee. On a ₹1 lakh personal loan it might earn ₹1,000 to ₹2,000 from the lender. Under the new MDR, a ₹5,000 payment at a large merchant could bring about ₹20 to be shared across banks and apps. Google does not report GPay India profit; these are rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Scratch-card rewards and referral bonuses in early years
Pre-installed or promoted on Android phones
Word of mouth: people need it to pay and receive money
growth.moat: GPay's moat is habit, Google trust and Android reach, plus being one of only two apps with huge scale. But UPI is open and free, so users can switch apps instantly, and the 30 percent cap, if enforced, could force it to shrink.

competitors.name: PhonePe

competitors.howThisProductDiffers: GPay is simpler and Google-backed; PhonePe has more merchants and products.

competitors.name: Paytm
competitors.positioning: Profitable payments company strong with merchant soundboxes.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Paytm earns more per merchant; GPay has more consumer users.

competitors.name: Navi, CRED and super.money

competitors.name: Bank apps and BHIM

competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Could gain if the cap pushes users from big apps.

pmLessons: Rewards can build a habit fast, but you must plan how to keep users when rewards shrink.
Regulation can decide your revenue. A rule like zero MDR, or a new MDR, changes the business overnight.
Being number two in a two-player market is still powerful, but rules can target both leaders.
Fees must be clear. Surprise fees cause more anger than the money itself.

interviewQuestions.question: Google Pay earns almost nothing from UPI. Why does Google run it?
interviewQuestions.hint: Mention strategic value: data, Android, ads and India as a test market. Then list direct revenue paths. Weigh both.

interviewQuestions.question: How should Google Pay respond to the 30 percent UPI market share cap?
interviewQuestions.hint: Discuss scenarios: cap enforced, delayed, softened. Plan for each: focus on value over volume, partnerships, lobbying.

interviewQuestions.question: A new 0.4 percent MDR applies to larger merchant payments. How would you launch it without losing merchants?
interviewQuestions.hint: Communicate clearly, show value, exempt small shops, offer tools like reports and loans. Track merchant churn and volume.

interviewQuestions.question: What would you build to win small merchants from PhonePe and Paytm?
interviewQuestions.hint: Understand merchant needs: alerts, settlement speed, loans. Propose one feature like a speaker or loan line. Define a metric.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the north star metric for Google Pay India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Habitual payers making several successful payments a month. Break into active payers, frequency, reliability and monetised users.
